purpose: Teach: 見舞わ/陥り/放つ/つながら/かけ離れ/一転/産む/傷つける

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、急なテストに見舞われたな
lines.en: Riku, you got hit with a surprise test, huh?
lines.style: Teasing lilt on the opening. Playful jab—not mean, but testing. Quick pace, knowing. A light smirk in the voice.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、落ち込みに陥りそうだぞ、桜
lines.en: You're gonna spiral into a funk over that, aren't you, Sakura?
lines.style: Steady, almost conspiratorial. Soft observation—he's seen this before. Slight warmth underneath the wry surface. No judgment.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、矢を放つアーチェリーが趣味だな
lines.en: So archery's your thing now, pulling back arrows and all?
lines.style: Genuine curiosity, without performance. Leaning in slightly. Warm attention. The tone of someone actually wanting to know.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、wifiがつながらないとイライラするな、桜
lines.en: You get all wound up when the wifi doesn't work, don't you, Sakura?
lines.style: Dry observation delivered with a half-smile in the voice. Affectionate callout. Light and unbothered, like he's won a point.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、理想とかけ離れた現実に悩んでたな
lines.en: You were really stressed about how far apart reality was from what you wanted.
lines.style: Quieter now. Serious but not heavy. Recognition of something that mattered. The shift is gentle, holding space for what he noticed.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、模試の結果が一転して良かったな、桜
lines.en: Your mock exam scores came through for you. That's good.
lines.style: Genuine warmth here. Simple and direct—not overdoing the praise but not hiding it either. Steady delivery, sincere.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前ん家の猫が子を産むんだろ
lines.en: Your cat's gonna have kittens soon, right?
lines.style: Bright interest. Simple, conversational. The kind of question that says he was listening before. No performance, just curiosity.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、人を傷つける言葉は使うなよ、桜
lines.en: Don't use words that hurt people, okay, Sakura?
lines.style: Firm but not angry. The tone of someone setting a boundary that matters. Direct eye-contact level. Not lecturing—protecting something.
